slides.0.title: Introducing wine of the Northwest and East Coast
slides.0.subtitle: The history and modern development of three states
slides.1.title: Oregon: from pioneers to a Pinot Noir name
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Pioneers of the 1960s
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Richard Sommer opened HillCrest near Roseburg in 1961 and sold his first vintage in 1964; David Lett planted Eyrie Vineyards near Dundee in the mid-1960s (sources say 1965 or 1966)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: International recognition in 1979
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Eyrie's 1975 South Block Pinot Noir placed in the top ten at the 1979 Gault-Millau French Wine Olympiades and was rated the top Pinot Noir; in a rematch arranged by Drouhin, Joseph Drouhin's 1959 Chambolle-Musigny narrowly won
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Rapid growth
slides.1.highlights.2.content: In 1970 there were 5 bonded wineries and 35 acres in production; in 1990, 70 wineries and 5,682 acres; the 2024 census counted 1,076 wineries and 47,343 planted acres
slides.1.content: Oregon's story is a few pioneers betting on Pinot Noir in the 1960s, winning international recognition in 1979 and then growing fast.
slides.2.title: Washington: from the Columbia Valley to Walla Walla
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The forerunner of Ste. Michelle
slides.2.highlights.0.content: American Wine Growers was founded in 1934 and grew into Chateau Ste. Michelle, rebranded in 1967
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Walla Walla pioneers
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Leonetti (1977), Quilceda Creek (1979), Woodward Canyon (1981), L'Ecole No. 41 (1983)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The first AVAs
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Yakima Valley became Washington's first AVA in 1983; Walla Walla Valley and Columbia Valley were both approved in 1984
slides.2.content: Washington started with a large producer; AVAs arrived in the 1980s, and small Walla Walla wineries built a boutique image.
slides.3.title: New York: the East Coast's oldest wine industry
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Where the Finger Lakes began
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The first vines were planted in Hammondsport in 1829; there were more than 50 wineries by 1900
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Konstantin Frank
slides.3.highlights.1.content: He emigrated in 1951, joined Cornell's Geneva station in 1953, bought land on the west side of Keuka Lake in 1958 and released his first vintage in 1962 (a Johannisberg Riesling Trockenbeerenauslese), showing that Vitis vinifera can survive cold climates
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The Farm Winery Act of 1976
slides.3.highlights.2.content: In 1976 the state had 19 wineries, all in the Finger Lakes and Long Island; by 1985 those two regions had 63
slides.3.content: New York's modern turning points were Frank showing vinifera could work, and the 1976 law lowering the bar for small wineries.
In which year did Richard Sommer open HillCrest?
1961; the first vintage went on sale in 1964.
In which year was New York's Farm Winery Act passed?
1976; the state then had only 19 wineries.
